findings.title: The security migration and outer-claim transaction are not yet an exact reviewable contract

source_refs.section: existing bound-writer function and trigger scope

findings.mechanism: The proposal defers numeric migration slot, exact trigger/preflight/claim-caller design and checksum to the lead before canonical approval. Existing 0029 has no outbox_events/outbox_attempts writer guard. Adding guards to those rows changes the outer claim transaction before the handler and the lock graph: an outer claimant can already hold the event lock while native bound writers lock parent then event. The candidate supplies intended outcomes and GUC names but no exact trigger lookup/locking behavior, candidate predicate placement, unsupported-row behavior, transaction GUC initialization point, renewal/ACK/fail coverage, or trigger/dependency ordering. A requirement to reject old claims is not that executable design.
findings.impact: A canonical human would be approving unresolved security/schema choices; a later trigger or claim implementation could consume attempts, block all claims, introduce lock inversion, or bypass generation checks. These are possible consequences, not observed runtime failures.
findings.required_resolution: Have the lead supply the concrete additive migration design and assigned numeric slot, ordered trigger/function/preflight inventory, exact immutable protocol lookup and per-writer transaction plan, including parent/event lock behavior and old-claim rollback. Freeze that candidate before exact human review; no migration implementation or DDL was authored by I1.

rejecting_oracles.procedure: Review the exact proposed migration and actual outer claimant/renewal/ACK/fail callers together. Reject unresolved trigger targets, unsupported-row/attempt behavior, GUC initialization, lock order, migration slot or prerequisite ordering.

After proper BUILD authority, an old ordinary claimant with valid old217 context must mutate zero event/attempt/lease/receipt rows on a complete binding. Race native parent-first writer against actual outer claim; reject partial attempt consumption, deadlock-driven successful fallback, downgrade or missing generation checks. A generation2 worker must still claim and settle complete and legacy cases.

findings.title: One-owner RESPONSE accounting does not assign all actual charge and result paths

source_refs.section: existing output guard transforms ModelResult.text and usage
one owner and existing native RESPONSE accounting

findings.mechanism: The delta explicitly replaces native preModel increment and postModel aggregate charging, which is a legitimate proposed change to224, but the copied response caller also directly adds inputTokens/outputTokens/costUsd in the unrecorded result-log-failure branch. That third write is outside the described two-site replacement. The candidate does not give a source-bound outcome contract that decides reserve/settle/UNKNOWN and this direct mutation for completed, unrecorded, failed, deadline and cancelled paths, or binds the raw ModelResult versus guarded text across the existing transforming published gateway. The actual runModelCall/kernel owner, LoopRun orchestration and checkpoint transition validator implementations are absent from the allowlist. Their reconciliation is explicitly deferred.
findings.impact: A plausible implementation that changes only the named pre/post gates can retain an extra token/cost debit on log failure, or validate/result-hash the wrong text. I1 does not assert that the unimplemented opted-in mode already double-charges, nor that missing sources are defective.
findings.required_resolution: Complete the source-bound per-outcome ownership contract, including the direct unrecorded debit, result-log failure after reserve/settle, raw result versus guarded response digests, acceptedDecision/acceptedResponse validation and receipt lifecycle. Supply the causal native owner/validator copies in a refreshed packet; preserve the non-opted-in paths. Do not add a second accounting layer.

rejecting_oracles.procedure: For each response pipeline outcome, identify every writer of modelCalls/inputTokens/outputTokens/costUsd and receipt status, and the authoritative result bytes. Reject any path where both admitted usage and the unrecorded direct additions apply, or where a gateway return bypasses qualification/receipt validation.

After approval, fail the real result log after valid native model return, with settlement committed, rolled back and ACK-lost variants. From independent persisted receipts, assert one modelCall and either exact settled usage once or conserved reservation once; no direct extra addition, second receipt, output acceptance on failure, or altered legacy accounting.

findings.title: The sole complete checkpoint phase has no constrained settlement classification

source_refs.section: run settlement gate and activePhase checks
terminal settlement and live successful close contract

findings.mechanism: Every new CAS, including terminal and UNKNOWN writes, requires phaseType complete.checkpoint; commitKind distinguishes only CHECKPOINT_ONLY and RESUME_POINT. The current native settlement allowlist admits step.saveCheckpoint but not complete.checkpoint, and both continuation.run and store.beginPhase classify permission by that list. Terminal wrappers close dispatch before the checkpoint await; recovered FAULTED/OPEN is settlement-only. Merely forwarding the new phase encounters the active-only guard. Broadly adding the phase to settlement would also admit nonterminal reservation/seal requests unless the delta defines a restricted transition validator. The phrase existing settlement-only exception does not choose the new classification, actor/cancellation route or allowed next-state changes.
findings.impact: Terminal success checkpoint/UNKNOWN recovery can be rejected after local close, or an overbroad repair can allow active progress through a settlement fence. This is a specified-contract gap, not a reproduced runtime failure. Retaining RESERVED when diagnostic CAS is unavailable remains a valid fail-closed fallback.
findings.required_resolution: Specify how complete CAS participates in active versus terminal/diagnostic settlement, including phase creation/ACK ownership, allowed ledger/state deltas, FAULTED and cancellation behavior, synchronous dispatch closure and retention of RESERVED when authority is absent. Settlement must never authorize a new reservation, seal, model, body or recovered success.

rejecting_oracles.procedure: Evaluate the exact phase/guard transition table for a healthy terminal checkpoint, UNKNOWN diagnostic after fault, cancelled-parent closure and missing settlement authority. Reject an unrecognized phase, recursive or duplicate ACK, active-dispatch gate after terminal closure, or a settlement transition permitting nonterminal progress.

After approval, prove healthy final terminal CAS+close succeeds; RESERVED recovery under a valid settlement fence preserves charge and stops; denied diagnostic CAS retains RESERVED and stops. Attempt reservation/RESUME_POINT under FAULTED/cancelled/closed settlement and require zero model/body/seal. Losing old fence cannot mutate winner.

findings.title: Define the scope and reset authority of synthetic pair disqualification

source_refs.section: existing registry is reconstructed on resolution

findings.mechanism: The pair is instantiated per execution, while a breach must mark the pair unqualified for future admissions. The proposed owner, lifetime and reset/requalification rule are not identified. Do not infer persistence or process-wide quarantine from a per-execution object.
findings.impact: A subsequent execution or restarted worker might immediately reconstruct a qualified instance. The frozen proof can fail red on breach without claiming a durable fleet quarantine.
findings.required_resolution: Clarify whether disqualification is a local proof verdict, process latch or persisted serving gate; label its scope and reset authority and align acceptance claims accordingly.

rejecting_oracles.procedure: After inducing ADMISSION_BREACH, attempt the next admission and, if cross-restart quarantine is claimed, restart the worker. Reject automatic qualification within the claimed quarantine scope.
